[ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Calling it a noble Qur’an glorifies and confirms the preceding oath. | mentions 56:75
[ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The parenthetical لو تعلمون falls between the adjective and the noun and intensifies the glorification; its unanswered conditional either denies their knowledge or implies that they would revere it or act accordingly.
[ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The greatness of the oath has been indicated earlier, and is especially clear if مواقع النجوم is understood as Ibn Abbas and others transmitted. | mentions 56:75
[ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الطيبي | reports | Al-Tibi explains كريم as excellent and pleasing among its kind of books, or as abundantly beneficial; the benefit fits a Qur’an containing foundational knowledge for this life and the next, with generosity used metaphorically.
[ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Another view takes generosity broadly to include praiseworthy qualities such as great benefit, making the description literal.
[ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | It may also mean noble in God’s sight; the author says this returns to the prior sense and requires an unnecessary implied preposition.
[ALUSI-FULL:v27p153#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The pronoun refers to the Qur’an itself, not merely to its status as a recitation; the point is that it was revealed to the Prophet rather than composed by him, as disbelievers claimed.
[ELMALILI:56:75-96#2/r8] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Karīm can mean richly beneficial because the Qur’an contains key knowledge for life and the afterlife, beautiful and worthy of honor, or honored with God.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The pronoun in “it is a noble Quran” has no expressed antecedent because the Quran is already mentally present to the audience.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p332/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Karim means precious and exalted; the Quran surpasses earlier divine books through comprehensive guidance, evidence, refutation, clarity, concision, eloquence, and sound. | mentions 27:29
[TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Other verses depict the Qur'an as preserved in a guarded tablet, an exalted wise source, and a protected book; its meanings rest on enduring, unchanging realities.
